scope: Source-only comparative audit of 0xShug0/audio.cpp as a second native C++/ggml/GGUF runtime challenger for Frankenstein 2.0 local German voice. Determine whether its broader shared ASR/TTS/VAD/model surface adds a non-duplicate target discriminator beyond the completed CrispASR consolidation audit and the NeMo-Speech.cpp candidate. No VPS execution, model download, runtime, German benchmark, integration or Trigger-4 acceptance credit is implied.
main_result: audio.cpp is admitted as a source-only comparative native-runtime challenger because v0.7.0 exposes Qwen3-ASR, Nemotron/Voxtral realtime ASR, Qwen3-TTS and several German-capable TTS/VAD families behind one C++/ggml/GGUF framework. It receives no shared-memory, latency, German-quality or target-runtime credit from source breadth alone.
critical_gap: Qwen3-TTS is not marked Stream in the v0.7.0 support table, so the released runtime does not yet prove a complete low-latency Qwen3-ASR + Qwen3-TTS voice path.
next_gate: After the canonical T7-SYS-002 post-repair clay-direct-dev hardware receipt, benchmark pinned audio.cpp v0.7.0 against the pinned NeMo-Speech.cpp and CrispASR/reference runtime paths using equivalent artifacts where possible; measure concurrent RSS/VRAM, p50/p95/p99, German quality, cancellation correctness and network-blocked operation.
